assessment.summary: BTK is one of the most thoroughly validated and druggable kinase targets in oncology and immunology, with 170 PDB structures (best resolution 1.08Å), over 21,000 ChEMBL IC50 entries, and six approved inhibitors including covalent (ibrutinib, acalabrutinib, zanubrutinib, tirabrutinib) and non-covalent (pirtobrutinib) agents. The target has strong disease validation across B-cell malignancies and autoimmune conditions, with active ongoing research into next-generation inhibitors and PROTACs. There are essentially no evidence gaps — this is a fully characterised, clinically proven drug target.
evidence_gaps: Resistance mechanisms to non-covalent inhibitors (e.g., pirtobrutinib) are still being characterised in real-world settings
Optimal patient selection biomarkers beyond BTK mutation status remain incompletely defined
Long-term safety profiles of newer-generation inhibitors in non-oncology indications (e.g., autoimmune disease) are still emerging
